transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I started eating cleaner for the lieutenant track, but it’s kind of turned into cutting meals way down. Some days, even on shift, it’s just black coffee, a protein shake, and a small dinner, even though I know I’ve burned a lot more than that.
Despite eating so little, do you find yourself feeling an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?
Yeah. If the scale’s up even a pound after a big station meal or just drinking more water, I get this tight panic feeling—like I’ve blown it, and people are going to see me as soft or out of control.
Could you tell me your current height and how much you weigh right now?

I don’t have the exact number in my head right now. I do know my gear and station clothes are hanging a lot looser, and the fitness review said my weight was too low for my build. But, honestly, part of me still thinks I could stand to trim down a little more.
Have you noticed any significant decrease in your sex drive or, if applicable, any disruption to your menstrual cycle since losing weight?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything specific like that, at least not enough that I’ve paid attention to it.
If applicable to you, are your monthly menstrual periods still coming regularly?
That doesn’t apply to me—I’m male.
Have you noticed any difficulty getting or keeping an erection since your weight dropped?
I haven’t really noticed a problem with that. It’s not something I’ve been paying much attention to, though.
Roughly how much weight have you lost since you started cutting back on your food?

I’m not sure of the exact number. My gear and station clothes are definitely hanging looser, and the fitness review said my weight was too low for my build. Still… part of me feels like I could stand to lose a little more.
Do you push yourself to exercise excessively or beyond what is needed for your job in order to burn calories and lose weight?
I’m not really sure what counts as excessive. I do the physical training required for work, but I haven’t specifically been trying to add exercise just to burn calories.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or taken things like laxatives or diet pills to keep your weight down?
No, I haven’t done anything like that.
Have you ever taken water pills or diuretics to try to reduce your weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by water pills. I haven’t taken anything specifically to reduce my weight.
Do you make a conscious effort to avoid foods that you consider high in fat or fattening?

Yeah, I guess I do. It started as trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track, but now I’m cutting meals down a lot—black coffee, a protein shake, then a small dinner—even on shift days when I know I’ve burned way more than that.
Have you had any blood tests done that showed abnormal hormone levels, such as low testosterone?
I don’t think so. I haven’t had any bloodwork that I know showed anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits marked food restriction, fear of weight gain, and body image distortion leading to significant weight loss (weight noted to be too low for build during fitness review). However, the characteristic endocrine disturbance required for a full diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (e.g., erectile dysfunction, loss of sexual potency) is absent, meeting criteria for atypical anorexia nervosa (F50.1).

confirmed_symptoms: Severe dietary restriction avoiding fattening foods
Intense fear of weight gain and panic over small scale fluctuations
Distorted body image (desire to trim down further despite being under recommended weight)
Objectively low body weight noticed via loose gear and fitness review

additional_requirements: Absence of secondary endocrine disorder (no reported erectile dysfunction or confirmed hormone abnormalities)
